Moraga.headline: Moraga: Cold start before afternoon rain returns
Moraga.text: Moraga starts cold and mostly quiet, with the latest archived KCAMORAG71 reading at 39°F around 1:38 AM and a sampled low of 37°F; the station feed has not refreshed through dawn, so that is the last verified snapshot, not a live reading. Clouds thicken today, and the NWS expects a chance of afternoon rain as a weak front moves southeast, with highs in the mid-50s. Showers may linger Sunday, while Monday looks like the clearest break. A stronger, wetter system is forecast Tuesday into Wednesday, with Bay shoreline flood warnings beginning Monday.

Lafayette.headline: Lafayette: Chilly morning gives way to afternoon rain chances
Lafayette.text: Lafayette starts chilly, with patchy fog possible in sheltered spots before clouds increase. The NWS expects mostly cloudy skies and a chance of rain this afternoon, with highs in the mid-50s; another chance of showers arrives Sunday, though coverage should be lighter. Monday looks like the clearest break. A stronger system is forecast Tuesday into Wednesday, bringing more widespread rain and breezier conditions, while exceptionally high Bay tides create a separate flooding concern along low-lying shoreline communities during Thanksgiving week.

Danville.headline: Danville: Cold valley start before showers return this afternoon
Danville.text: Danville starts cold, with patchy morning fog possible and sheltered locations near the upper 30s. The NWS expects mostly cloudy skies and a chance of rain Saturday afternoon, with highs in the mid-50s; Sunday stays cloudy with another morning rain chance and only a slight chance later. Monday looks like a relative lull. Rain becomes more likely Tuesday and Wednesday, so check gutters and drainage around low spots before the next Pacific system arrives this week.

Greenbrook.headline: Danville: Greenbrook faces a cold start and afternoon rain chance
Greenbrook.text: Danville's Greenbrook area starts cold, with patchy fog possible in sheltered parts of the valley before clouds thicken. The NWS forecast for the interior East Bay calls for a chance of rain Saturday afternoon and highs in the mid-50s, followed by a cloudy Sunday with another morning shower chance. Monday should be a useful lull. A stronger system is forecast Tuesday into Wednesday, bringing more widespread rain and breezier conditions while already-wet ground remains vulnerable to runoff.

Marin City.headline: Marin City: Afternoon rain approaches as Bay tides climb
Marin City.text: Marin City has a cool, relatively quiet start, but clouds build and rain becomes possible this afternoon and evening as a weak front crosses the Bay Area. Showers may linger Sunday, while Monday offers a brief lull before rain and stronger southerly winds return Tuesday into Wednesday. The bigger local concern is the Bay shoreline flood warning from Monday morning through Thursday afternoon, coinciding with exceptionally high tides. Watch low-lying waterfront access and follow posted closures; tide timing differs around the Bay.

Sausalito.headline: Sausalito: Waterfront prepares for king tides and a wetter holiday week
Sausalito.text: Sausalito starts cool and mostly quiet, with clouds increasing before a chance of rain arrives this afternoon and evening. A few showers may linger Sunday, followed by a relative lull Monday; a stronger Pacific system is forecast Tuesday into Wednesday. The main waterfront concern is the coastal flood warning for Bay shorelines from Monday morning through Thursday afternoon, when very high tides may combine with storm-driven water levels. Keep marina approaches and low-lying roads in mind, and follow local closure notices.

Brentwood.headline: Brentwood: Chilly Delta morning before a chance of afternoon rain
Brentwood.text: Brentwood starts cold, with patchy fog possible around the Delta and low-lying roads before clouds increase. The NWS expects mostly cloudy skies and a chance of rain Saturday afternoon, with highs in the mid-50s; Sunday remains cloudy with only a modest rain chance. Monday is the best dry break. A stronger system is forecast Tuesday and Wednesday, bringing more widespread rain and breezier conditions, while saturated ground from this week's storms keeps runoff and drainage worth watching.

East Sacramento.headline: East Sacramento: Cold, fog-prone morning before light rain returns
East Sacramento.text: East Sacramento starts cold, with patchy fog possible in the Valley, although the densest current advisory is farther south in the northern San Joaquin Valley through 10 AM. A weaker system brings light rain later Saturday into Sunday; most Valley totals should stay light, while the mountains pick up snow above 4,000 feet. Monday briefly dries out. A stronger system returns Tuesday through Thanksgiving, but NWS Sacramento says it should be less wet than the midweek storm just passed.
